name: Zeughaus Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: Built around 1500 by Emperor Maximilian I, the Zeughaus in Innsbruck showcases Tyrolean cultural history within its imposing Renaissance quadrangle.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Zeughaus in Innsbruck (historically also known as Kaiserliches Zeughaus) is situated on the banks of the Sill River in the Dreiheiligen district at approximately 575 metres above sea level. Built around 1500 by Emperor Maximilian I as a military arsenal, the monumental four-wing complex with its expansive courtyard is one of the most significant surviving Renaissance secular buildings in Austria. Today, the complex houses a branch of the Tiroler Landesmuseen and invites visitors on a captivating journey through the cultural and technological history of Tyrol.

History & Collections

Emperor Maximilian I. chose Innsbruck as his primary residence and systematically upgraded the city into the military centre of his empire. Between 1500 and 1506, he commissioned the construction of the Zeughaus directly on the Sill in order to centrally store and maintain artillery, siege weapons, and war materiel. The waters of the Sill powered grinding and polishing mills; renowned cannon founders such as Peter Löffler cast cannons of European renown here. The massive quadrangular complex with two two-storey wings and two gate buildings measures an impressive 80 by 100 metres. Following centuries of military use as barracks and a depot, the ensemble was extensively restored and opened to the public as a museum in 1973. The permanent exhibition vividly illustrates the historical development of Tyrol: from prehistory and early history through the golden age of mining and coinage to the 1809 liberation struggles and the pioneering achievements of Tyrolean alpinism.

Visit & Getting There

The museum in the Zeughaus is open Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (closed on Mondays). Admission prices (as of 2025/2026): Regular €9.00, reduced €7.00, children and youths up to 19 years enjoy free admission. Entry is free of charge with the all-inclusive Innsbruck Card. In summer, the atmospheric courtyard serves as a venue for the popular Zeughaus-Open-Air-Kino. Arrival by public transport: From Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof take tram lines 1 or 3 to the Messe/Zeughaus stop, or bus line R to Dreiheiligenstraße (approx. 3–5 minutes on foot). By car: Via motorway A12, exit Innsbruck Ost, towards Messe/Zentrum; paid parking is available in the surrounding streets or at the Messe underground car park.

Tips

The spacious inner courtyard and the ground-floor exhibition areas are barrier-free and wheelchair accessible; a lift provides access to the upper floors. For families in particular, the museum's educational armoury and tool collection is a highlight, offering interactive insights into historical craft techniques. After your museum visit, enjoy a scenic walk along the Sill promenade all the way to its confluence with the Inn River.
